newsitem.title: USA: DC panel to address city's "decaying" buildings.
newsitem.headline: DC panel to address city's "decaying" buildings.

text.p: The District of Columbia's financial control board said on Monday it will issue recommendations for dealing with the city's "decaying" schools, roads and bridges by April 30.
The panel said in a draft 25-page report scheduled for release in final form on Thursday that the city's infrastructure maintenance and replacement program is "in ruin."
The board said bond firms on Wall Street will play a key role in helping the city finance much-needed improvements.
"Clearly, the financial markets are looking to the District to provide evidence of improvement in order to respond positively to future borrowings," the report says.

The panel said it "has begun a process to improve communications with the municipal finance community." It said it will issue a report by March 31 on the District's "financial management structure and capacity, along with major recommendations for change."
The panel said a continued exodus of businesses and residents from D.C. is hampering efforts to stabilize District finances.
It said it will examine barriers to economic development, hold public hearings and present recommendations aimed at "stemming the tide of migration" by June 30.
The panel said "archaic" personnel rules inherited by the city in the mid-1970s when D.C. shifted to Home Rule are also a major obstacle to the city's financial success.
The board will address the way the city recruits, pays and evaluates workers in a reform plan due out by April 30, the panel said.

The panel said it has reviewed over 2,400 city contracts since November 1995 and found "little improvement" in contract processing. It said it will issue a report on the state of the city's contracting operations by February 28.
